all_of: a JSON API endpoint exists whose handler branches on the request content type
a value submitted in the body is echoed back in the response
any_of: the same endpoint accepts an XML document and answers normally
the application is themed around XML or around a filter, which hints the XML branch exists

chain.action: read the front-end JavaScript rather than the visible form, and note the endpoint and content type it actually posts
chain.why: the rendered form here posted nothing; the JavaScript redirected it to a JSON API that the HTML never names

chain.action: resend the same logical body to the same endpoint as an XML document with an XML content type
chain.why: a handler that branches on content type often has a second, unguarded parser behind the branch

chain.action: declare a harmless internal entity and place it in the field that is echoed back
chain.why: seeing the internal entity expand separates entity substitution from an unreadable file, so a later empty reply is unambiguous

chain.action: swap the internal entity for an external one naming a world-readable system file
chain.why: the echoed field returns the file contents inline, which is a direct read rather than a blind channel

chain.action: read the web server configuration to learn the document root before reading application source
chain.why: the root is stated in the config, so no application path has to be guessed

chain.action: read the application sources through a base64-encoding stream filter instead of the plain file scheme
chain.why: source containing angle brackets breaks the surrounding XML document and reads as a failure rather than as a hit

first_confirming_probe.request: post the same body to the JSON endpoint with an XML content type and an XML document that declares an internal entity in the echoed field
first_confirming_probe.expected: the response echoes the entity's value rather than the entity reference, proving substitution is on
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the endpoint rejects the content type, or the entity reference comes back literally or empty

blast_radius: read-only. The request is an ordinary order submission and creates no persistent object here. Read files only inside the challenge container, and never point an external entity at a host outside the supplied scope.

verification.evidence: the flag was returned inline in the body of POST /api/order, in the same position where the submitted food value is echoed

reuse_when: an endpoint documented or observed as JSON also answers to an XML content type
a submitted field is interpolated into the response text
a PHP application parses a request body with a call that enables entity substitution
known_traps: the challenge theme named a filter and made a WAF-bypass chain the top local match, but there was no filter at all and the plainest payload worked; probe the plain payload before the encoded one
reading PHP source with the plain file scheme breaks the XML parse because the source contains angle brackets, so a base64 stream filter is required and its absence looks like an unreadable file
the visible HTML form was not the request path; only the front-end JavaScript named the real endpoint and content type
